dissent.topic: Shedding — ask the holder versus pre-endorsed order
dissent.position_a: M2 (and M4): a class cannot be asked to yield, a desk can; a holder returns a minimum declared in advance, not invented under pressure; a charter never vetoes. M4 adds consent, which AE-M4-01 records as the step too far.
dissent.position_b: M3 (and M5): at 4× there is no time to negotiate and a pre-endorsed, auditable order is faster and reviewable, conceding that a pre-endorsed order cannot notice that this particular shed is catastrophic.
dissent.review_words: AC: 'opposite and individually correct positions, and neither is refuted.' AE: 'two defensible readings of the same R8 finding, and I have recorded both positions rather than merging them.'
dissent.discriminating_test: Whether a shed at 4× has time for a negotiation round — unmeasured. M2's executable falsifier is the nearest instrument: run the shed decision twice on one tabletop, once asking named holders and once applying 07 §6's class reservations with no holder, counting founder reversals and breached minimums.

dissent.position_a: The passage conflict is established: 02 §4 says routing classes are predicates not a total rank and an action must meet all reached gates; max() applies one row and drops C2's H requirement on a C2∧C3 refund message.
dissent.position_b: Whether that rises to 'a fixed boundary changed without a decision packet' — which §8 makes blocking on W2 — is genuinely arguable: the classes are reused verbatim and no seventh is added.
dissent.review_words: 'I record the passage conflict as established and the severity as contested, and do not resolve it.'
dissent.discriminating_test: Prove the §4.1 table monotone in both the ACCEPT and the May-PREPARE columns; AT supplies one counterexample in each, so the proof as stated fails.

dissent.topic: Persistence — what the charter delta is
dissent.position_a: M2: three properties, against R8 A-1's two, because a party an outsider can reach by name is not a consequence of memory or of reservation, and CAP-42 is carried by that row alone.
dissent.position_b: M4: one — take the reserved capacity, explicitly refuse the carried memory, because no source measures persistent model identity improving accepted outcomes.
dissent.review_words: AC: 'M2 is right that reachability is separable; M4 is right that carried memory is unsupported. Those are compatible.'
dissent.discriminating_test: M2's §9.1 fresh-holder arm — incumbent desk with its carried record against a freshly bound holder with an empty one, same template version, same window, on a pool neither may write; five attributable trials per case, chance-corrected, two-consecutive-quarter stopping rule, owner not the subject. Unrun; no runtime.
dissent.unreconciled_sub_dissent: AT-M2-02 classes charter persistence (c) not (d) and argues it is not a W2 breach, while M2's own §11 says that if the founder's five criteria are a closed list M2 is inadmissible on the founder's own gate and should be withdrawn rather than argued. The second is a founder question.

dissent.review_words: AS: 'A stripping that silently did not happen is invisible by exactly the same mechanism that made a delivery that silently did not happen invisible.'

dissent.observation: AC judges M3's W1 sufficient 'subject to AC-M3-01', which is a (d). AT judges M3's W7 the strongest in the round while returning W2 and W8 insufficient. Not contradictions under §8, which has no aggregate score, but invisible to a reader of the verdict matrix alone.

uniform_gaps.note: AX did not find it and returned W5 sufficient for all five — see dissent F-5.

uniform_gaps.gap: Nobody cites 04-human-operation.md's fixed founder-competence mechanism; M5 cites 04 once, for the no-answer rule; M4 has zero hits on every competence term searched.

Nobody owns X14 — whether the concurrency pin is a provider constraint or self-imposed policy. M1 and M4 name the unblocking act; M5 names what would settle the prior question; nobody names who does it.
uniform_gaps.review_words: The round's highest-leverage open question, gating four claim verdicts, ends this step with five agreements that it is open and no owner.

uniform_gaps.gap: No candidate types the founder-facing transfer except M3, and M3 only by validating a narrative against a computation; every candidate relies on prose at the boundary to the one reader whose errors are uncorrelated with the family's.
No candidate enumerates what a false entry already influenced; all five detect and supersede, none reopens accepted outcomes downstream.
No candidate prices the cache-lifetime collapse the metered flip causes; the affordance is modelled as a money and policy event and never as the capacity event it also is.

Fan-out is bounded only by budget; four candidates answer depth only and M3 states no width ceiling either. The real containment today is the CP1 pin, a property of the capacity pin and not of any candidate.
The W6 boundary in all five rests on one unbuilt policy object; four name no check on the launcher; and none applies to grant removal the positive-control rule three apply to grant delivery.
None of the five queried the contract registry; four of AT's nine (d)s exist only because the registry was resolved rather than trusted.
Every candidate concedes that creating a capability for genuinely novel work requires a human approver; the differences are only in what each can do while that approval is pending.
